summary.title: Baby's First Garbage Collector
summary.one_liner: You learn how a basic mark-and-sweep garbage collector works and how to write one in about a hundred lines of C for a toy VM with int and pair objects.
takeaways: An object is in use if a variable in scope references it, or an in-use object references it; everything else is garbage.
Mark-sweep works in two phases: mark all reachable objects from the VM stack roots, then walk a list of all allocations and free unmarked ones.
Marking must check for already-marked objects so cyclic pair references do not recurse forever.
The VM keeps its own linked list of every allocation so it can still find and free objects the program can no longer reach.
Triggering GC after a count of allocations, then setting the next threshold to twice the live object count, is a simple heuristic.
summary.summary: The author walks through building a mark-and-sweep garbage collector for a small dynamically typed language with ints and pairs, implemented in plain C. It starts with the reachability definition of garbage, then builds a tagged-union object type, a VM with an explicit stack, and the mark phase (with cycle protection). The sweep phase uses a linked list of all allocations to free unmarked objects. The post finishes with a simple allocation-count trigger and a heap threshold that doubles after each collection.
